statements.quote: GSE's registry has **68 word-scale primes** (the lexicon basis, `tier_0_dispatch`) and **29 sentence-scale operators** (`SENTENCE_SCALE` + the hierarchy markers: `SYN_*`, `COMP_*`, `INTENSITY`, `QUANTITY`, `HIER_PLUS/MINUS`, `CERTAINTY`). … | very | `INTENSITY` | / | much, many, all, some, (a) few, (a) little | `QUANTITY` (± `HIER_*`) | / | more, most; -er/-est | `HIER_PLUS` / `HIER_MAX` | … This is a deliberate, **named** computational adaptation of canonical NSM: strict NSM keeps `MUCH/MANY, ALL, SOME, VERY, MORE` as atomic *quantifier/intensifier primes*, whereas GSE (like Fähndrich 2014) realizes them as **scalar operators** (`QUANTITY`/`INTENSITY`/`HIER`).
